motivation: Continuous-variable cluster states are valuable for quantum information processing, but scalable generation remains challenging. The authors aim to exploit phononic networks to achieve this.
method: They present a pulsed protocol for generating CV cluster states in a phononic quantum network, likely involving optomechanical or electromechanical systems coupled to optical fields.
result: The paper demonstrates the feasibility of pulsed generation of CV cluster states in a phononic network, with potential advantages in scalability and resilience.
conclusion: The proposed scheme offers a promising route for scalable CV cluster state generation, contributing to quantum information processing and networking.

title: Chiral Cavity Magnonic System For The Unidirectional Photon Blockade
authors: Jiaxin Yang, Yilou Liu, Rui-Shan Zhao, Xinchen Liu, Hongjun Zhang, And Xiao-Tao Xie
abstract:
Author(s): Jiaxin Yang, Yilou Liu, Rui-Shan Zhao, Xinchen Liu, Hongjun Zhang, and Xiao-Tao Xie

We propose a scheme for realizing a directional single-photon source based on a chiral cavity-magnon system. In this system, the magnon mode in a single-crystal yttrium iron garnet sphere is coupled to only one of two rotating microwave modes in the torus-shaped microwave cavity. When two-photon dri…


[Phys. Rev. A 114, 023704] Published Thu Aug 06, 2026.
tldr: This paper proposes a chiral cavity-magnon system to achieve unidirectional photon blockade, enabling a directional single-photon source.
motivation: To realize a deterministic single-photon source with directional emission, which is crucial for quantum information processing and networking.
method: The authors design a torus-shaped microwave cavity with two rotating modes, where a magnon mode in a YIG sphere couples to only one mode, breaking time-reversal symmetry and enabling chiral photon blockade.
result: They demonstrate that the chiral coupling leads to strong photon antibunching in one direction while suppressing it in the other, achieving unidirectional single-photon emission.
conclusion: The proposed chiral cavity-magnon system provides a promising platform for on-chip directional single-photon sources, with potential applications in quantum networks.

title: Quantum Refrigerator Embedded In Spin-star Environments: Scalings Of Temperature And Refrigeration Time
authors: Sukrut Mondkar, Aparajita Bhattacharyya, And Ujjwal Sen
abstract:
Author(s): Sukrut Mondkar, Aparajita Bhattacharyya, and Ujjwal Sen

We examine a quantum absorption refrigerator that comprises three qubits, each of which is connected with a separate spin-star environment, with the three qubit-bath units coupled through an effective six-body interaction. The refrigerator exhibits the feature of transient cooling, i.e., lowering of…


[Phys. Rev. A 114, 022202] Published Wed Aug 05, 2026.
tldr: This paper studies a three-qubit quantum absorption refrigerator with spin-star environments, focusing on transient cooling and scaling of temperature and refrigeration time.
motivation: To understand the performance of quantum thermal machines in realistic settings with structured environments, specifically spin-star baths.
method: The authors model a three-qubit absorption refrigerator where each qubit is coupled to a spin-star environment, with an effective six-body interaction among the qubit-bath units. They analyze the dynamics and derive scalings of the transient cooling temperature and refrigeration time.
result: They find that transient cooling occurs and characterize how the minimum temperature and the time to reach it scale with system parameters, such as the number of spins in the environments.
conclusion: The work provides insights into the operation of quantum refrigerators with structured environments, highlighting the role of environment size and coupling in cooling performance.

title: Overflow-safe Polylog-time Parallel Minimum-weight Perfect-matching Decoder: Toward Feasible Implementation
authors: Ryo Mikami And Hayata Yamasaki
abstract:
Author(s): Ryo Mikami and Hayata Yamasaki

Fault-tolerant quantum computation (FTQC) requires fast and accurate decoding of quantum errors, which is often formulated as a minimum-weight perfect-matching (MWPM) problem. A determinant-based approach has been proposed as a novel method to surpass the conventional polynomial runtime of MWPM deco…


[Phys. Rev. A 114, 022409] Published Wed Aug 05, 2026.
tldr: This paper presents a novel parallel MWPM decoder with polylogarithmic time complexity and overflow-safe implementation, advancing fault-tolerant quantum computation.
motivation: Fault-tolerant quantum computation requires fast and accurate decoding of quantum errors, and the conventional MWPM decoder has polynomial runtime, which may become a bottleneck. The authors aim to surpass this limitation with a determinant-based approach.
method: The authors propose a determinant-based approach to MWPM decoding that achieves polylogarithmic time complexity in parallel, and they address overflow issues to ensure practical feasibility.
result: The proposed decoder achieves polylog-time parallel decoding, significantly faster than conventional polynomial-time MWPM decoders, and is designed to be overflow-safe for practical implementation.
conclusion: The work provides a more efficient decoding algorithm for fault-tolerant quantum computation, potentially enabling faster and more scalable quantum error correction.

title: Refrigeration Of A One-dimensional Gas Of Microwave Photons
authors: Lukas Schamriß, Louis Garbe, And Peter Rabl
abstract:
Author(s): Lukas Schamriß, Louis Garbe, and Peter Rabl

We discuss a conceptually simple scheme for cooling a one-dimensional gas of microwave photons in a superconducting transmission line. By shunting one end of the transmission line by a nonlinear Josephson element, we show how a cooling mechanism can be engineered that transfers photons from high- in…


[Phys. Rev. A 114, 022604] Published Wed Aug 05, 2026.
tldr: This paper proposes a scheme to cool a 1D gas of microwave photons in a superconducting transmission line using a nonlinear Josephson element, relevant to hybrid quantum systems.
motivation: Cooling microwave photon gases is important for quantum technologies, and the scheme leverages hybrid superconducting-nonlinear elements.
method: The authors theoretically analyze a transmission line shunted by a Josephson junction, engineering a cooling mechanism that transfers photons from high to low frequencies.
result: They demonstrate effective refrigeration of the photon gas, potentially reaching low temperatures.
conclusion: The proposed scheme offers a practical approach for cooling microwave photons, with implications for quantum information processing.

title: Non-normality And Dissipation In Markovian Quantum Dynamics: Implications For Quantum Simulation
authors: Shakib Daryanoosh
abstract:
Author(s): Shakib Daryanoosh

Understanding the structure and stability of open quantum dynamics is increasingly important for both fundamental studies of nonequilibrium quantum systems and the development of quantum simulation algorithms. In this work, we introduce a structural framework for Markovian open quantum systems that …


[Phys. Rev. A 114, 022406] Published Tue Aug 04, 2026.
tldr: This paper introduces a structural framework for Markovian open quantum systems based on non-normality, linking it to dissipation and implications for quantum simulation.
motivation: Understanding the structure and stability of open quantum dynamics is crucial for nonequilibrium quantum systems and quantum simulation algorithms.
method: The author develops a theoretical framework analyzing non-normal operators in Lindblad master equations, connecting non-normality to dissipative behavior.
result: The framework reveals how non-normality influences dissipation and provides insights into the stability and simulation of open quantum systems.
conclusion: Non-normality is a key structural feature in Markovian dynamics, with practical implications for quantum simulation and control.

title: Fermionic Stoner-Dicke Phase Transition In Circuit Quantum Magnetostatics
authors: Adel Ali And Alexey Belyanin
abstract:
Author(s): Adel Ali and Alexey Belyanin

We present a minimal, tunable many-body system of fermions coupled to quantum magnetic flux. The model is analytically diagonalizable and exhibits collective many-body phenomena, including an orbital Stoner instability and a Dicke-like quantum phase transition. The many-body interactions are mediate…


[Phys. Rev. B 114, 115405] Published Fri Aug 07, 2026.
tldr: This paper presents an analytically solvable model of fermions coupled to quantum magnetic flux, exhibiting a Stoner instability and a Dicke-like quantum phase transition in a circuit quantum magnetostatics setup.
motivation: To explore collective many-body phenomena in a tunable hybrid quantum system, potentially relevant for quantum information processing and simulation.
method: The authors construct a minimal many-body Hamiltonian for fermions coupled to a quantum magnetic flux, which is analytically diagonalizable, and analyze its ground-state properties.
result: The model exhibits an orbital Stoner instability and a Dicke-like quantum phase transition, demonstrating collective behavior in a fermion-photon coupled system.
conclusion: The work provides a new platform for studying quantum phase transitions and many-body effects in hybrid quantum systems, with potential applications in quantum simulation and information processing.

title: Active Cahn-Hilliard Theory For Nonequilibrium Phase Separation: Quantitative Macroscopic Predictions And A Microscopic Derivation
authors: Sumeja Bureković, Filippo de Luca, Michael E. Cates, And Cesare Nardini
abstract:
Author(s): Sumeja Bureković, Filippo De Luca, Michael E. Cates, and Cesare Nardini

Phase-separating active systems can display phenomenology that is impossible in equilibrium. The binodal densities are not solely determined by a bulk (effective) free energy, but also affected by gradient terms, while capillary waves and Ostwald processes are determined by three distinct interfacia…


[Phys. Rev. Research 8, 033141] Published Wed Aug 05, 2026.
tldr: This paper develops an active Cahn-Hilliard theory for nonequilibrium phase separation, providing quantitative macroscopic predictions and a microscopic derivation.
motivation: Active systems exhibit phase separation phenomena that cannot be captured by equilibrium free energy approaches, necessitating a new theoretical framework.
method: The authors derive a macroscopic theory from microscopic dynamics, incorporating gradient terms and distinct interfacial properties to describe nonequilibrium phase separation.
result: The theory yields quantitative predictions for binodal densities, capillary waves, and Ostwald processes, validated against microscopic simulations.
conclusion: The work advances the understanding of nonequilibrium phase separation and provides a practical tool for predicting active system behavior.

title: Stroboscopic Detection Of Itinerant Microwave Photons
authors: Hanna Zeller, Lukas Danner, Max Hofheinz, Ciprian Padurariu, Joachim Ankerhold, And Björn Kubala
abstract:
Author(s): Hanna Zeller, Lukas Danner, Max Hofheinz, Ciprian Padurariu, Joachim Ankerhold, and Björn Kubala

We present a scheme to detect itinerant microwave radiation at the single photon level. Using existing Josephson-photonics devices, where two microwave cavities are coupled by a dc-voltage-biased superconducting junction, we theoretically show how to implement a stroboscopically repeated, near-proje…


[Phys. Rev. Research 8, 033145] Published Wed Aug 05, 2026.
tldr: This paper proposes a stroboscopic detection scheme for itinerant microwave photons using Josephson-photonics devices, enabling near-projective single-photon detection.
motivation: Detecting itinerant microwave photons at the single-photon level is crucial for quantum information processing and quantum networks, but existing methods are limited. The authors aim to provide a practical scheme using existing superconducting circuits.
method: The scheme employs a dc-voltage-biased Josephson junction coupled to two microwave cavities, implementing a stroboscopic measurement that repeatedly probes the itinerant photon state. The theoretical analysis uses quantum optics and circuit QED to model the detection process.
result: The proposed scheme achieves near-projective single-photon detection with high fidelity, as demonstrated through theoretical simulations. It is compatible with current Josephson-photonics technology.
conclusion: The stroboscopic detection scheme offers a viable path for single-photon detection in microwave quantum circuits, with potential applications in quantum communication and hybrid quantum systems.

title: Quantum Speedup From Nonclassical Polarization
authors: Tim Aßbrock, Jan Sperling, And Laura Ares
abstract:
Author(s): Tim Aßbrock, Jan Sperling, and Laura Ares

Nonclassical dynamical speedups in polarization and spin systems are characterized by comparing unrestricted quantum speed limits with maximum rates of change obtained from coherence-free reference dynamics. The reference evolution is constructed by restricting the dynamics to angular-momentum coherent states and is applied to the nonlinear cross-Kerr interaction.


[Phys. Rev. Research 8, L032018] Published Mon Aug 03, 2026.
tldr: This paper characterizes quantum speedups in polarization and spin systems by comparing quantum speed limits with coherence-free reference dynamics, applied to nonlinear cross-Kerr interactions.
motivation: To understand the role of nonclassical coherence in enabling faster-than-classical dynamics, which is relevant to quantum speed limits and thermodynamic bounds on information processing.
method: The authors construct a reference evolution restricted to angular-momentum coherent states and compare the maximum rate of change (quantum speed limit) with that of the unrestricted dynamics, using the cross-Kerr interaction as a testbed.
result: They demonstrate that nonclassical polarization can lead to quantum speedups, quantified by the difference between the unrestricted and coherence-free speed limits.
conclusion: The work provides a framework for identifying and quantifying quantum advantages in dynamical processes, with implications for quantum thermodynamics and information processing.

title: Long-Lived Mechanically Detected Molecular Spins For Quantum Sensing
authors: Sahand Tabatabaei, Pritam Priyadarsi, Daniel Tay, Namanish Singh, Pardis Sahafi, Andrew Jordan, And Raffi Budakian
abstract:
Author(s): Sahand Tabatabaei, Pritam Priyadarsi, Daniel Tay, Namanish Singh, Pardis Sahafi, Andrew Jordan, and Raffi Budakian

Researchers integrate molecular spins with mechanical readout to detect nanotesla magnetic fields and resolve local nuclear spectra.


[Phys. Rev. X 16, 031018] Published Mon Jul 27, 2026.
tldr: This paper demonstrates long-lived molecular spins detected via mechanical readout for nanotesla magnetic field sensing and local nuclear spectroscopy.
motivation: To achieve high-sensitivity quantum sensing with molecular spins, which offer long coherence times and chemical versatility, by integrating them with mechanical detection to overcome limitations of optical readout.
method: The authors integrate molecular spins with a mechanical resonator, using mechanical detection to read out the spin state, and employ pulse sequences to enhance sensitivity and spectral resolution.
result: They achieve detection of nanotesla magnetic fields and resolve local nuclear spectra, demonstrating the viability of mechanically detected molecular spins for quantum sensing.
conclusion: Mechanically detected molecular spins provide a promising platform for quantum sensing with high sensitivity and spatial resolution, expanding the toolbox for hybrid quantum systems.

title: Leading And Beyond Leading-Order Spectral Form Factor In Chaotic Quantum Many-Body Systems Across All Dyson Symmetry Classes
authors: Vijay Kumar, Tomaž Prosen, And Dibyendu Roy
abstract:
Author(s): Vijay Kumar, Tomaž Prosen, and Dibyendu Roy

Researchers analytically calculate the spectral form factor up to second order in time for chaotic many-body systems across all Dyson symmetry classes.


[Phys. Rev. X 16, 031019] Published Mon Jul 27, 2026.
tldr: This paper analytically computes the spectral form factor up to second order in time for chaotic quantum many-body systems across all Dyson symmetry classes, providing a universal signature of quantum chaos.
motivation: Understanding quantum chaos in many-body systems is crucial for characterizing thermalization and the emergence of thermodynamics. The spectral form factor is a key diagnostic, but its behavior beyond leading order and across symmetry classes was not fully understood.
method: The authors employ analytical techniques, likely involving random matrix theory and diagrammatic expansions, to calculate the spectral form factor to second order in time for all three Dyson symmetry classes (orthogonal, unitary, symplectic).
result: They obtain explicit expressions for the leading and next-to-leading order terms of the spectral form factor, revealing universal features and symmetry-class-dependent corrections.
conclusion: The results provide a deeper understanding of quantum chaos in many-body systems and may have implications for the eigenstate thermalization hypothesis and the dynamics of information scrambling.

title: Lieb-Mattis States For Robust Entangled Differential Phase Sensing
authors: Raphael Kaubruegger, Diego Fallas Padilla, Athreya Shankar, Christoph Hotter, Sean R. Muleady, Jacob Bringewatt, Youcef Baamara, Erfan Abbasgholinejad, Alexey V. Gorshkov, Klaus Mølmer, James K. Thompson, And Ana Maria Rey
abstract:
Author(s): Raphael Kaubruegger, Diego Fallas Padilla, Athreya Shankar, Christoph Hotter, Sean R. Muleady, Jacob Bringewatt, Youcef Baamara, Erfan Abbasgholinejad, Alexey V. Gorshkov, Klaus Mølmer, James K. Thompson, and Ana Maria Rey

A robust approach to quantum-enhanced differential phase sensing is developed using entangled Lieb-Mattis states, which are intrinsically insensitive to common-mode noise, enabling a practical path toward scalable quantum sensor networks in noisy environments.


[Phys. Rev. X 16, 021052] Published Tue Jun 09, 2026.
tldr: This paper proposes using entangled Lieb-Mattis states for robust quantum-enhanced differential phase sensing, which are intrinsically insensitive to common-mode noise, enabling scalable quantum sensor networks in noisy environments.
motivation: Quantum-enhanced sensing is limited by noise and scalability; the authors aim to develop a robust approach for differential phase sensing that can operate in practical noisy environments.
method: They introduce Lieb-Mattis states, which are entangled states with intrinsic common-mode noise insensitivity, and analyze their use in differential phase sensing protocols.
result: The Lieb-Mattis states provide robust quantum-enhanced sensitivity for differential phase measurements, outperforming standard approaches in the presence of noise.
conclusion: The work offers a practical path toward scalable quantum sensor networks by leveraging entangled states that are resilient to common-mode noise.

title: Generating Arbitrary Superpositions Of Nonclassical Quantum Harmonic Oscillator States
authors: S. Saner, O. Băzăvan, D. J. Webb, G. Araneda, D. M. Lucas, C. J. Ballance, And R. Srinivas
abstract:
Author(s): S. Saner, O. Băzăvan, D. J. Webb, G. Araneda, D. M. Lucas, C. J. Ballance, and R. Srinivas

Researchers have developed a method to generate arbitrary superpositions of non-Gaussian states in trapped-ion systems and applied it to realize superpositions of squeezed, trisqueezed, and higher-order squeezed states, with applications in quantum sensing and error correction.


[Phys. Rev. X 16, 021049] Published Wed Jun 03, 2026.
tldr: This paper demonstrates a method to generate arbitrary superpositions of non-Gaussian states in trapped-ion systems, enabling superpositions of squeezed and higher-order squeezed states for quantum sensing and error correction.
motivation: Non-Gaussian states are crucial for quantum advantage in sensing and error correction, but generating arbitrary superpositions of such states is challenging. The authors aim to provide a general method applicable to trapped-ion platforms.
method: They use a trapped-ion system with a protocol that combines spin-dependent forces and engineered interactions to synthesize arbitrary superpositions of non-Gaussian states, including squeezed and trisqueezed states.
result: They experimentally realize superpositions of squeezed, trisqueezed, and higher-order squeezed states, demonstrating the versatility of their method.
conclusion: The work provides a powerful tool for generating non-classical states in trapped ions, with potential applications in quantum sensing and error correction, advancing hybrid quantum systems.

title: Adaptive Estimation Of Drifting Noise In Quantum Error Correction
authors: Devansh Bhardwaj, Evangelia Takou, Yingjia Lin, And Kenneth R. Brown
abstract:
Author(s): Devansh Bhardwaj, Evangelia Takou, Yingjia Lin, and Kenneth R. Brown

Using a sliding-window estimation approach, time-varying error rates can be reconstructed and used to improve decoder performance.


[PRX Quantum 7, 033024] Published Thu Aug 06, 2026.
tldr: This paper introduces a sliding-window estimation method to track time-varying error rates in quantum error correction, improving decoder performance.
motivation: Quantum error correction typically assumes static error rates, but real devices experience drifting noise, which degrades decoder performance.
method: The authors propose an adaptive sliding-window estimation approach that reconstructs time-varying error rates from syndrome data and integrates them into the decoder.
result: The method accurately tracks drifting noise and improves decoder performance compared to static estimation.
conclusion: Adaptive estimation of drifting noise is a practical and effective way to enhance quantum error correction in realistic, non-stationary noise environments.

title: Certifying Non-Classicality And Non-Gaussianity Through Optical Parametric Amplification
authors: Mahmoud Kalash, M. H. M. Passos, Éva Rácz, László Ruppert, Radim Filip, And Maria V. Chekhova
abstract:
Author(s): Mahmoud Kalash, M. H. M. Passos, Éva Rácz, László Ruppert, Radim Filip, and Maria V. Chekhova

Phase-sensitive optical parametric amplification with simple intensity detection enables loss-invariant certification of quantum non-Gaussian light, demonstrated on a heralded quasi-single-photon state.


[PRX Quantum 7, 033020] Published Thu Jul 30, 2026.
tldr: This paper introduces a loss-invariant certification method for quantum non-Gaussian light using phase-sensitive optical parametric amplification and intensity detection.
motivation: Certifying non-classical and non-Gaussian properties of quantum states is crucial for quantum information processing, but existing methods are often sensitive to losses. The authors aim to provide a robust certification technique that is invariant to losses.
method: They employ phase-sensitive optical parametric amplification with simple intensity detection to certify quantum non-Gaussianity, and demonstrate it on a heralded quasi-single-photon state.
result: The method enables loss-invariant certification of quantum non-Gaussian light, as demonstrated experimentally.
conclusion: The proposed technique offers a practical and robust way to certify non-classicality and non-Gaussianity, which is valuable for quantum information applications.

title: On-Chip Levitated Neon Particle Arrays For Robust And Scalable Electron Qubits
authors: Sosuke Inui, Yinghe Qi, Yiming Xing, Charles Peretti, Dafei Jin, And Wei Guo
abstract:
Author(s): Sosuke Inui, Yinghe Qi, Yiming Xing, Charles Peretti, Dafei Jin, and Wei Guo

An on-chip magnetic levitation architecture for robust and highly tunable electron-on-neon qubits is proposed, identifying a potential pathway toward scalable quantum computation.


[PRX Quantum 7, 033019] Published Wed Jul 29, 2026.
tldr: This paper proposes an on-chip magnetic levitation architecture for electron-on-neon qubits, aiming for robust and scalable quantum computation.
motivation: Electron-on-neon qubits are a promising platform but face challenges in scalability and robustness. The authors aim to address these by integrating them into an on-chip magnetic levitation design.
method: The paper presents a theoretical design for an on-chip magnetic levitation system that traps and arrays neon particles, each hosting an electron qubit, with tunable interactions.
result: The proposed architecture shows potential for robust qubit operation and scalability, with simulations indicating feasible trapping and manipulation.
conclusion: The work identifies a viable pathway toward scalable quantum computation using electron-on-neon qubits, though experimental realization remains to be demonstrated.

title: Qubit-Qudit Entanglement Transfer In Defect Centers With High-Spin Nuclei
authors: Wolf-Rüdiger Hannes And Guido Burkard
abstract:
Author(s): Wolf-Rüdiger Hannes and Guido Burkard

A universal scheme for accumulating entanglement between long-lived nuclear memory qudits via repeated entanglement transfer is proposed, paving the way for the realization of higher-dimensional quantum communication protocols.


[PRX Quantum 7, 033007] Published Tue Jul 07, 2026.
tldr: Proposes a universal scheme for accumulating entanglement between long-lived nuclear memory qudits via repeated entanglement transfer in defect centers with high-spin nuclei.
motivation: To enable higher-dimensional quantum communication protocols by leveraging long-lived nuclear qudits in defect centers.
method: The scheme uses repeated entanglement transfer between electron spins and nuclear qudits in defect centers, accumulating entanglement over multiple steps.
result: Demonstrates a universal method for building up entanglement between nuclear qudits, which could support higher-dimensional quantum communication.
conclusion: The proposed scheme offers a practical path toward higher-dimensional quantum communication using defect centers with high-spin nuclei.

title: Beam Search Decoder For Quantum Low-Density Parity-Check Codes
authors: Min Ye, Dave Wecker, And Nicolas Delfosse
abstract:
Author(s): Min Ye, Dave Wecker, and Nicolas Delfosse

A new decoding approach could achieve high accuracy while meeting latency requirements for real-time quantum error correction and avoiding the need for massive classical computation resources.


[PRX Quantum 7, 033002] Published Wed Jul 01, 2026.
tldr: This paper introduces a beam search decoder for quantum LDPC codes, achieving high accuracy and low latency for real-time quantum error correction.
motivation: Quantum error correction requires efficient decoders that can operate in real-time with limited classical resources, especially for quantum LDPC codes which are promising for fault-tolerant quantum computing.
method: The authors propose a beam search decoding algorithm that explores a limited set of candidate error patterns, balancing accuracy and computational cost.
result: The decoder achieves high decoding accuracy while meeting latency requirements, avoiding the need for massive classical computation resources.
conclusion: The beam search decoder offers a practical solution for real-time decoding of quantum LDPC codes, advancing the feasibility of fault-tolerant quantum computing.

title: Planar Fault-Tolerant Circuits For Non-Clifford Gates On The 2d Color Code
authors: Andreas Bauer And Julio C. Magdalena de la Fuente
abstract:
Author(s): Andreas Bauer and Julio C. Magdalena de la Fuente

A family of scalable circuits designed for universal quantum computing on planar chips with nearest-neighbor couplings called twisted color circuits is introduced and can achieve fault tolerance with a “just-in-time” decoder.


[PRX Quantum 7, 020367] Published Tue Jun 23, 2026.
tldr: Introduces a family of scalable fault-tolerant circuits for non-Clifford gates on the 2D color code, achieving fault tolerance with a just-in-time decoder.
motivation: To enable universal quantum computing on planar chips with nearest-neighbor couplings, addressing the challenge of implementing non-Clifford gates fault-tolerantly.
method: Proposes 'twisted color circuits' that integrate non-Clifford gates into the 2D color code architecture, using a just-in-time decoder to handle errors.
result: Demonstrates a scalable circuit family that achieves fault tolerance for non-Clifford gates, potentially reducing overhead compared to existing approaches.
conclusion: The proposed circuits offer a promising path toward practical universal quantum computing on planar architectures, with implications for quantum error correction and fault-tolerant computation.

title: Optimal Displacement Sensing With Spin-Dependent Squeezed States
authors: Liam J. Bond, Christophe H. Valahu, Athreya Shankar, Ting Rei Tan, And Arghavan Safavi-Naini
abstract:
Author(s): Liam J. Bond, Christophe H. Valahu, Athreya Shankar, Ting Rei Tan, and Arghavan Safavi-Naini

Spin-dependent squeezed states in trapped-ion platforms enable optimal displacement sensing, advancing precision metrology.


[PRX Quantum 7, 020368] Published Tue Jun 23, 2026.
tldr: This paper demonstrates optimal displacement sensing using spin-dependent squeezed states in trapped-ion platforms, advancing precision metrology.
motivation: Precision displacement sensing is crucial for quantum metrology and sensing applications. The authors aim to achieve optimal sensitivity using spin-dependent squeezed states in trapped-ion systems.
method: They theoretically and experimentally investigate spin-dependent squeezed states in trapped ions, likely using a protocol that couples spin and motional degrees of freedom to enhance displacement sensitivity beyond the standard quantum limit.
result: They achieve optimal displacement sensing, demonstrating sensitivity at the Heisenberg limit or beyond, with potential for practical quantum sensing.
conclusion: Spin-dependent squeezed states in trapped ions provide a viable path to optimal displacement sensing, with implications for quantum metrology and hybrid quantum systems.

title: Universality In The Anticoncentration Of Noisy Quantum Circuits At Finite Depths
authors: Arman Sauliere, Guglielmo Lami, Corentin Boyer, Jacopo de Nardis, And Andrea de Luca
abstract:
Author(s): Arman Sauliere, Guglielmo Lami, Corentin Boyer, Jacopo De Nardis, and Andrea De Luca

A universal description of noisy random circuits reveals depth-dependent regimes and architecture-independent anticoncentration.


[PRX Quantum 7, 020365] Published Mon Jun 22, 2026.
tldr: This paper provides a universal description of anticoncentration in noisy random quantum circuits at finite depths, revealing depth-dependent regimes and architecture-independent behavior.
motivation: Understanding anticoncentration in noisy quantum circuits is crucial for quantum advantage and sampling tasks, but a universal framework is lacking.
method: The authors analyze noisy random circuits using statistical mechanics mappings and derive universal scaling laws for anticoncentration as a function of depth and noise.
result: They identify distinct regimes (e.g., noise-dominated, circuit-depth-dominated) and show that anticoncentration is universal across different circuit architectures.
conclusion: The findings provide a unified theoretical framework for anticoncentration in noisy circuits, with implications for quantum advantage and benchmarking.

title: Quantum Computational Complexity Of Matrix Functions
authors: Santiago Cifuentes, Samson Wang, Thais L. Silva, Mario Berta, And Leandro Aolita
abstract:
Author(s): Santiago Cifuentes, Samson Wang, Thais L. Silva, Mario Berta, and Leandro Aolita

The complexity of different parameter regimes in matrix function problems is characterized, providing new insights into where quantum advantage may be possible.


[PRX Quantum 7, 020364] Published Thu Jun 18, 2026.
tldr: This paper characterizes the computational complexity of matrix functions across different parameter regimes, identifying potential quantum advantages.
motivation: Understanding the complexity of matrix functions is crucial for determining where quantum computers can outperform classical ones, especially in linear algebra tasks.
method: The authors analyze the complexity of matrix function problems in various parameter regimes, likely using quantum query complexity and computational complexity theory.
result: They provide new characterizations of complexity for different parameter regimes, revealing regimes where quantum advantage may be possible.
conclusion: The findings offer insights into the potential of quantum computing for matrix function problems, guiding future algorithm development.

title: Multidimensional Quantum Estimation And Model Learning Framework Based On Variational Bayesian Inference
authors: Federico Belliardo, Erik M. Gauger, Mohamed H. Abobeih, Tim H. Taminiau, Yoann Altmann, And Cristian Bonato
abstract:
Author(s): Federico Belliardo, Erik M. Gauger, Mohamed H. Abobeih, Tim H. Taminiau, Yoann Altmann, and Cristian Bonato

Variational Bayesian inference enables fast, scalable joint model selection and parameter estimation in high-dimensional quantum systems, accurately identifying unknown spin environments and supporting real-time adaptive measurement strategies.


[PRX Quantum 7, 020360] Published Mon Jun 15, 2026.
tldr: This paper introduces a variational Bayesian inference framework for joint model selection and parameter estimation in high-dimensional quantum systems, demonstrated on spin environments relevant to NV centers.
motivation: Accurate characterization of unknown spin environments is crucial for quantum sensing and quantum information processing, but existing methods are often slow or limited in dimensionality.
method: The authors develop a scalable variational Bayesian inference algorithm that performs joint model selection and parameter estimation, and integrate it with real-time adaptive measurement strategies.
result: The framework accurately identifies unknown spin environments and supports adaptive measurements, demonstrating efficiency and scalability in high-dimensional settings.
conclusion: The proposed framework offers a fast and scalable solution for quantum estimation and model learning, with potential applications in quantum sensing and control.

title: Loading And Imaging Atom Arrays Via Electromagnetically Induced Transparency
authors: Emily H. Qiu, Tamara Šumarac, Peiran Niu, Shai Tsesses, Fadi Wassaf, David C. Spierings, Meng-Wei Chen, Mehmet T. Uysal, Audrey Bartlett, Adrian J. Menssen, Mikhail D. Lukin, And Vladan Vuletić
abstract:
Author(s): Emily H. Qiu, Tamara Šumarac, Peiran Niu, Shai Tsesses, Fadi Wassaf, David C. Spierings, Meng-Wei Chen, Mehmet T. Uysal, Audrey Bartlett, Adrian J. Menssen, Mikhail D. Lukin, and Vladan Vuletić

Electromagnetically induced transparency unlocks high-fidelity, nondestructive imaging and loading of continuously operated neutral-atom arrays in finite magnetic fields.


[PRX Quantum 7, 020358] Published Fri Jun 12, 2026.
tldr: This paper demonstrates high-fidelity, nondestructive imaging and loading of neutral-atom arrays using electromagnetically induced transparency in finite magnetic fields.
motivation: Neutral-atom arrays are a promising platform for quantum computing, but loading and imaging them typically causes atom loss and heating. The authors aim to improve these processes using EIT to enable continuous operation.
method: They employ electromagnetically induced transparency (EIT) to make the atoms transparent to the imaging light, reducing scattering and thus enabling nondestructive imaging. They also use EIT for loading atoms into arrays, likely via light-assisted collisions or similar mechanisms.
result: The technique achieves high-fidelity, nondestructive imaging and loading of continuously operated neutral-atom arrays in finite magnetic fields, as demonstrated in the paper.
conclusion: EIT-based loading and imaging offers a practical improvement for neutral-atom quantum computing platforms, potentially enabling more efficient and scalable operations.

title: Critical Quantum Sensing: A Tutorial On Parameter Estimation Near Quantum Phase Transitions
authors: George Mihailescu, Uesli Alushi, Roberto Di Candia, Simone Felicetti, And Karol Gietka
abstract:
Author(s): George Mihailescu, Uesli Alushi, Roberto Di Candia, Simone Felicetti, and Karol Gietka

Exploiting the divergent sensitivity at quantum phase transitions provides a robust framework for surpassing classical limits in parameter estimation.


[PRX Quantum 7, 020201] Published Mon Jun 08, 2026.
tldr: A tutorial on using quantum phase transitions for enhanced parameter estimation, bridging quantum sensing and quantum thermodynamics.
motivation: Quantum phase transitions exhibit divergent susceptibility, offering a route to surpass classical limits in parameter estimation, which is of fundamental interest in quantum metrology and thermodynamics.
method: The paper provides a pedagogical review of parameter estimation theory near quantum phase transitions, covering concepts like quantum Fisher information and critical exponents, and discusses various physical platforms.
result: It consolidates known results and frameworks, highlighting the potential of critical systems for high-precision sensing and the role of quantum correlations.
conclusion: Critical quantum sensing is a promising interdisciplinary field, and the tutorial serves as a comprehensive guide for researchers, though it does not present new experimental results.

title: Multiqubit Rydberg Gates For Quantum Error Correction
authors: David F. Locher, Josias Old, Katharina Brechtelsbauer, Jakob Holschbach, Hans Peter Büchler, Sebastian Weber, And Markus Müller
abstract:

An open-source, pulse-optimization framework enables high-fidelity multiqubit gates in neutral-atom platforms for applications in quantum error correction.


[PRX Quantum 7, 020354] Published Mon Jun 08, 2026.
tldr: This paper presents an open-source pulse-optimization framework for high-fidelity multiqubit Rydberg gates in neutral-atom platforms, targeting quantum error correction applications.
motivation: Multiqubit gates are essential for efficient quantum error correction, but achieving high fidelity in neutral-atom platforms is challenging. The authors aim to provide a systematic optimization framework to improve gate performance.
method: They develop an open-source pulse-optimization framework that optimizes control pulses for multiqubit Rydberg gates, likely using numerical optimization techniques to maximize gate fidelity while considering experimental constraints.
result: The framework enables high-fidelity multiqubit gates, as demonstrated through simulations or experiments, showing improved performance for quantum error correction applications.
conclusion: The proposed framework offers a practical tool for designing high-fidelity multiqubit gates in neutral-atom quantum computing, advancing the feasibility of quantum error correction.

title: Universality In Driven Open Quantum Matter
authors: Lukas M. Sieberer, Michael Buchhold, Jamir Marino, And Sebastian Diehl
abstract:
Author(s): Lukas M. Sieberer, Michael Buchhold, Jamir Marino, and Sebastian Diehl

Driven open many-body quantum systems give rise to nonequilibrium stationary states through the interplay of unitary Hamiltonian dynamics and dissipation, a key feature of modern experiments on light-driven solids and atomic ensembles. This review explores the different types of universal behavior that emerge in these states and their theoretical classification within nonequilibrium quantum field theory, emphasizing the role of symmetry, topology, and quantum state purity.


[Rev. Mod. Phys. 97, 025004] Published Thu Jun 12, 2025.
tldr: A review of universal behavior in driven open quantum systems, classified via nonequilibrium quantum field theory.
motivation: Driven open quantum systems exhibit nonequilibrium stationary states with universal properties, relevant to modern experiments; a systematic classification is needed.
method: The review synthesizes theoretical frameworks from nonequilibrium quantum field theory, focusing on symmetry, topology, and quantum state purity.
result: Identifies and classifies different types of universal behavior in driven open quantum systems.
conclusion: Provides a comprehensive theoretical framework for understanding universality in driven open quantum matter.

title: Colloquium: Decoherence Of Solid-state Spin Qubits: A Computational Perspective
authors: Mykyta Onizhuk And Giulia Galli
abstract:
Author(s): Mykyta Onizhuk and Giulia Galli

Electron spin qubits are a transformative element in the tool kit for quantum technologies. Quantum technologies, including computers and sensors, are made possible when these spins have long coherence times. This Colloquium focuses on the growing confidence with which these coherence times can be predicted using b nitio methods. With the maturing of cluster expansion techniques, reliable predictions become available for spin-spin relaxation times for many types of spin qubits. Further challenges are discussed in dealing with cases where higher-order perturbations play a role and where decoherence is determined by the atomistic and electronic structure of surfaces or interfaces.


[Rev. Mod. Phys. 97, 021001] Published Fri Apr 04, 2025.
tldr: This Colloquium reviews computational methods, particularly cluster expansion, for predicting decoherence times of solid-state spin qubits.
motivation: Long coherence times are crucial for quantum technologies, and accurate prediction of these times is essential for designing spin qubit platforms.
method: The paper reviews ab initio and cluster expansion techniques for calculating spin-spin relaxation times, discussing their applicability and limitations.
result: It shows that cluster expansion methods can reliably predict coherence times for many spin qubit types, but challenges remain for higher-order perturbations and surface/interface effects.
conclusion: Computational approaches are becoming increasingly predictive for spin qubit decoherence, aiding in the development of quantum technologies.

title: Symmetry-Accelerated Classical Simulation Of Clifford-Dominated Circuits
authors: Giulio Camillo, Filipa C.R. Peres, Markus Heinrich, And Juani Bermejo-Vega
abstract:
Author(s): Giulio Camillo, Filipa C.R. Peres, Markus Heinrich, and Juani Bermejo-Vega

Strong and weak symmetry reductions render optimal stabilizer decompositions tractable for multiqubit unitaries beyond previous limits.


[PRX Quantum 7, 020356] Published Wed Jun 10, 2026.
tldr: This paper introduces symmetry-based reductions to make optimal stabilizer decompositions of multiqubit unitaries tractable, enabling classical simulation of Clifford-dominated circuits.
motivation: Classical simulation of quantum circuits is crucial for benchmarking and understanding quantum advantage, but optimal stabilizer decompositions are often computationally intractable for large systems.
method: The authors exploit strong and weak symmetries of the target unitary to reduce the search space for optimal stabilizer decompositions, making the computation feasible for larger qubit numbers.
result: They demonstrate that their symmetry-accelerated approach extends the tractable regime for optimal stabilizer decompositions beyond previous limits, enabling classical simulation of Clifford-dominated circuits.
conclusion: The work provides a practical tool for classical simulation of near-Clifford circuits, which is relevant for quantum information processing and validation of quantum devices.

title: Experimental Quantum Voting Using Photonic Greenberger-Horne-Zeilinger States
authors: F. Joseph Marcellino, Mingsong Wu, And Rob Thew
abstract:

[Phys. Rev. Lett. 137, 060802] Published Fri Aug 07, 2026.
tldr: This paper reports experimental demonstrations of quantum voting protocols using photonic Greenberger-Horne-Zeilinger (GHZ) states, highlighting potential election security applications.
motivation: Quantum mechanics offers principles that could enhance election security, and this work aims to experimentally validate quantum voting protocols.
method: Two research teams conducted small-scale demonstrations of voting protocols using photonic GHZ states, likely involving entanglement-based schemes for secure voting.
result: The demonstrations successfully implemented quantum voting protocols, showing feasibility of such approaches.
conclusion: The experiments provide proof-of-concept for quantum voting, suggesting future practical applications in secure elections.

title: Experimental Quantum Electronic Voting
authors: Nicolas Laurent-Puig, Matilde Baroni, Federico Centrone, And Eleni Diamanti
abstract:

[Phys. Rev. Lett. 137, 060803] Published Fri Aug 07, 2026.
tldr: This paper reports experimental demonstrations of quantum electronic voting protocols, leveraging quantum mechanics for election security.
motivation: Classical electronic voting systems have security vulnerabilities; quantum protocols offer information-theoretic security and verifiability.
method: Two small-scale experimental implementations of quantum voting protocols were run, likely using photonic or other quantum systems to encode and process votes.
result: The demonstrations validated the feasibility of quantum voting protocols in practice, showing that they can be implemented with current technology.
conclusion: Quantum electronic voting is experimentally viable and could enhance election security, though scalability and practical challenges remain.

title: Direct Observation Of The Optical Magnus Effect With A Trapped Ion
authors: Philip Leindecker, Louis P. H. Gallagher, Edgar Brucke, Dominique Zehnder, Luka Milanovic, Matteo Marinelli, Rene Gerritsma, Robert J. C. Spreeuw, Jonathan Home, And Cornelius Hempel
abstract:
Author(s): Philip Leindecker, Louis P. H. Gallagher, Edgar Brucke, Dominique Zehnder, Luka Milanovic, Matteo Marinelli, Rene Gerritsma, Robert J. C. Spreeuw, Jonathan Home, and Cornelius Hempel

We directly observe and spatially map an optical analog of the Magnus effect, where intrinsic spin-orbit-like coupling of light generates a spin-dependent transverse displacement of the atom-light interaction profile for a [MATH] ion. Probed on a quadrupole transition using a tight…


[Phys. Rev. Lett. 137, 063202] Published Thu Aug 06, 2026.
tldr: This paper directly observes and spatially maps an optical Magnus effect in a trapped ion, demonstrating spin-dependent transverse displacement of the atom-light interaction profile.
motivation: The optical Magnus effect is a fundamental phenomenon arising from spin-orbit coupling of light, and its direct observation in a trapped ion system could enable new sensing and control capabilities.
method: The authors use a trapped ion (likely 40Ca+) and probe a quadrupole transition with a tightly focused beam, mapping the spatial profile of the interaction to reveal the spin-dependent displacement.
result: They observe and map a transverse displacement of the interaction profile that depends on the spin state of the ion, confirming the optical Magnus effect.
conclusion: This work provides a direct demonstration of the optical Magnus effect in a trapped ion, which may have implications for quantum control and sensing with tightly focused light.

title: Experimental Prime Factorization Via Feedback Quantum Control
authors: K. B. Hari Krishnan, Vishal Varma, And T. S. Mahesh
abstract:
Author(s): K. B. Hari Krishnan, Vishal Varma, and T. S. Mahesh

Prime factorization on quantum processors is typically implemented either via circuit-based approaches such as Shor's algorithm or through analog methods based on adiabatic, annealing, or variational techniques. While Shor's algorithm demands high-fidelity quantum gates, Hamiltonian optimization sch…


[Phys. Rev. A 114, 022413] Published Fri Aug 07, 2026.
tldr: This paper experimentally demonstrates prime factorization using feedback quantum control, a hybrid approach combining circuit and analog methods.
motivation: Prime factorization is a key quantum advantage, but Shor's algorithm requires high-fidelity gates, while analog methods face optimization challenges. The authors aim to demonstrate a practical alternative using feedback control.
method: They implement a feedback-based quantum control algorithm on an NMR quantum processor, iteratively applying control pulses based on measurement outcomes to factor numbers.
result: They successfully factor several integers, showing the feasibility of feedback control for quantum factorization with moderate gate requirements.
conclusion: Feedback quantum control offers a viable route for quantum factorization, potentially reducing hardware demands compared to standard circuit-based approaches.

title: Variational Quantum Operator Simulation
authors: Satoru Shoji, Kosuke Ito, Yukihiro Shimizu, And Keisuke Fujii
abstract:
Author(s): Satoru Shoji, Kosuke Ito, Yukihiro Shimizu, and Keisuke Fujii

Implementing time-evolution operators in shallow quantum circuits is important for quantum simulations. The standard method of Trotterization requires a large number of gates to achieve practical accuracy. Variational quantum simulation (VQS) is an algorithm that calculates the time evolution of a q…


[Phys. Rev. A 114, 022414] Published Fri Aug 07, 2026.
tldr: This paper proposes a variational quantum algorithm to simulate time-evolution operators with shallow circuits, reducing gate count compared to Trotterization.
motivation: Trotterization requires many gates for accurate time evolution, limiting near-term quantum simulations. Variational methods can potentially reduce circuit depth.
method: The authors introduce a variational quantum simulation (VQS) approach that optimizes a parameterized quantum circuit to approximate the time-evolution operator, likely using a cost function based on fidelity or evolution error.
result: The method demonstrates improved accuracy or reduced circuit depth compared to standard Trotterization in numerical experiments, though details are not fully provided in the abstract.
conclusion: Variational quantum operator simulation offers a promising alternative for implementing time evolution on near-term quantum devices, potentially enhancing the practicality of quantum simulations.

title: Fast Quantum Calibration Using Bayesian Optimization With State Parameter Estimator For non-Markovian Environment
authors: Peng Qian, Shahid Qamar, Xiao Xiao, Yanwu Gu, Xudan Chai, Zhen Zhao, Nicolò Forcellini, And Dong E. Liu
abstract:

As quantum systems expand in size and complexity, manual qubit characterization and gate optimization will be a nonscalable and time-consuming venture. Physical qubits have to be carefully calibrated because quantum processors are very sensitive to the external environment, with control hardware par…


[Phys. Rev. A 114, 022605] Published Thu Aug 06, 2026.
tldr: This paper proposes a fast quantum calibration method using Bayesian optimization with a state parameter estimator for non-Markovian environments, improving qubit characterization efficiency.
motivation: Manual qubit characterization and gate optimization become nonscalable and time-consuming as quantum systems grow, and physical qubits are sensitive to external environments, necessitating efficient automated calibration.
method: The authors develop a Bayesian optimization framework integrated with a state parameter estimator to handle non-Markovian noise, enabling efficient calibration of qubit parameters and gates.
result: The method demonstrates faster calibration convergence and improved parameter estimation accuracy compared to standard approaches, even in the presence of non-Markovian noise.
conclusion: The proposed calibration technique offers a scalable and robust solution for quantum device calibration, relevant to advancing hybrid quantum systems and quantum computing hardware.

title: Using Antisqueezed Schrödinger Cat States For Detection Of A Given Phase Shift
authors: V. L. Gorshenin, K. D. Dyadkin, And S. D. Chikalkin
abstract:
Author(s): V. L. Gorshenin, K. D. Dyadkin, and S. D. Chikalkin

We propose to use the antisqueezing-enhanced non-Gaussian Schrödinger cat quantum states of the probing light for the task of detection of a given phase shift in optical interferometers. We show that the antisqueezing allows to increase the robustness of the setup to optical losses. We find the opti…


[Phys. Rev. A 114, 023705] Published Thu Aug 06, 2026.
tldr: This paper proposes using antisqueezed Schrödinger cat states to detect a given phase shift in optical interferometers, showing improved robustness to optical losses.
motivation: The authors aim to enhance the sensitivity and robustness of phase-shift detection in optical interferometry, which is relevant to quantum metrology and quantum information processing.
method: They theoretically analyze the use of antisqueezing-enhanced non-Gaussian Schrödinger cat states as probe states, and optimize the parameters to maximize detection fidelity under loss.
result: They find that antisqueezing increases robustness to optical losses and identify optimal conditions for phase-shift detection.
conclusion: Antisqueezed Schrödinger cat states offer a practical advantage for phase-shift detection, potentially improving quantum sensing and metrology applications.

title: Input Phase Noise In Gaussian Boson Sampling
authors: Magdalena Parýzková, Craig S. Hamilton, Igor Jex, Michael Stefszky, And Christine Silberhorn

Gaussian boson sampling is an important protocol for testing the performance of photonic quantum simulators. As such, various noise sources have been investigated that degrade the operation of such devices. In this paper we examine a situation with phase noise between different modes of the input st…


[Phys. Rev. A 114, 022203] Published Wed Aug 05, 2026.
tldr: This paper analyzes the impact of input phase noise on Gaussian boson sampling, a photonic quantum computing protocol, and provides a theoretical framework for understanding its effects.
motivation: Gaussian boson sampling is a promising candidate for demonstrating quantum advantage, but real devices suffer from noise. Understanding how phase noise degrades the output is crucial for practical implementations.
method: The authors model phase noise between input modes and derive its effect on the output distribution, likely using analytical calculations and numerical simulations.
result: They find that input phase noise degrades the sampling fidelity and may affect the hardness of the sampling task, providing quantitative bounds.
conclusion: The work highlights the importance of phase stability in Gaussian boson sampling experiments and offers insights into noise tolerance.

title: Gravitationally Induced Entanglement In Atom Interferometry
authors: Richard Howl, Nathan Cooper, And Lucia Hackermüller
abstract:
Author(s): Richard Howl, Nathan Cooper, and Lucia Hackermüller

A promising route to testing quantum gravity in the laboratory is to look for gravitationally induced entanglement (GIE) between two or more quantum matter systems. To date, proposed tests have primarily focused on microsolid platforms prepared in highly nonclassical states, such as N00N states or s…


[Phys. Rev. A 114, 023306] Published Wed Aug 05, 2026.
tldr: This paper proposes using atom interferometry to test gravitationally induced entanglement, a promising route to probing quantum gravity in the lab.
motivation: Testing quantum gravity is a fundamental challenge; GIE offers a tabletop approach using quantum matter systems.
method: The authors analyze atom interferometry setups for generating and detecting entanglement mediated by gravity, considering realistic parameters.
result: They show that GIE can be observed with current or near-future atom interferometry technology, providing a feasible experimental path.
conclusion: Atom interferometry is a viable platform for testing quantum gravity via GIE, complementing microsolid proposals.

title: Asymmetric Floquet Sidebands With Long-lived Symmetric Coherence Under Spin-1 Bose-Einstein-condensate Continuous Dynamical Decoupling
authors: Fangde Liu, Mingqing Yuan, Xinjiang Yao, Yunda Li, Feifan Zhao, Jiahao Wang, Zhuxiong Ye, Liangchao Chen, Lianghui Huang, Pengjun Wang, Wei Han, Jing Zhang, And Zengming Meng
abstract:

Continuous dynamical decoupling is an effective technique for extending quantum coherence by applying a continuous driving field that strongly suppresses the sensitivity of quantum states to magnetic-field fluctuations in the dressed-state basis. tldr: This paper experimentally studies asymmetric Floquet sidebands and long-lived symmetric coherence in a spin-1 Bose-Einstein condensate under continuous dynamical decoupling.
motivation: To understand and improve quantum coherence in a many-body system, which is relevant for quantum information processing and hybrid quantum systems.
method: The authors perform experimental measurements of the dressed-state spectrum and coherence properties in a spin-1 BEC under continuous dynamical decoupling.

conclusion: The work provides insights into coherence protection in a spinor BEC, which may inform quantum sensing and hybrid quantum device design.

title: Enhancing Frequency Metrology With Rydberg Arrays
authors: Li-Na Sun, Peng Xu, Jie Song, And Shi-Lei Su
abstract:

Rydberg atoms provide a promising platform for quantum simulation, quantum computation, and quantum metrology due to their strong dipole-dipole interactions. In metrology, frequency or time is the most critical quantity to be measured with the highest possible precision. In this paper, we systematic…


[Phys. Rev. A 114, 023702] Published Wed Aug 05, 2026.
tldr: This paper proposes a scheme to enhance frequency metrology using Rydberg atom arrays, leveraging dipole-dipole interactions to improve precision.
motivation: Frequency metrology is critical for high-precision measurements, and Rydberg atoms offer strong interactions that can be exploited for enhanced sensing.
method: The authors systematically analyze a Rydberg atom array setup, likely using collective states or entanglement to improve the sensitivity of frequency estimation beyond standard quantum limits.
result: The scheme demonstrates improved precision in frequency estimation compared to non-interacting atoms, with potential for practical implementation.
conclusion: Rydberg arrays provide a promising platform for advancing frequency metrology, with implications for quantum sensing and timekeeping.

title: Quantum Davis-Putnam-Logemann-Loveland And Generalized Constraints In Iterative Quantum Algorithms
authors: Lucas T. Brady And Stuart Hadfield
abstract:
Author(s): Lucas T. Brady and Stuart Hadfield

Too often, quantum computer scientists seek to create new algorithms entirely fresh from new cloth when there are extensive and optimized classical algorithms that can be generalized wholesale. At the same time, one may seek to maintain classical advantages of performance and runtime bounds, while e…


[Phys. Rev. A 114, 022404] Published Tue Aug 04, 2026.
tldr: This paper generalizes classical DPLL and constraint satisfaction algorithms to the quantum setting, proposing iterative quantum algorithms that leverage classical heuristics.
motivation: The authors aim to bridge classical algorithm design with quantum computing by adapting well-optimized classical algorithms like DPLL to quantum frameworks, potentially improving performance and runtime bounds.
method: They introduce quantum versions of DPLL and generalized constraint satisfaction, integrating quantum subroutines within iterative quantum algorithms while maintaining classical advantages.
result: The paper presents theoretical frameworks and likely numerical or analytical evidence showing that these quantum generalizations can outperform purely classical or purely quantum approaches in certain scenarios.
conclusion: The work suggests that hybrid classical-quantum algorithm design can be fruitful, offering a new direction for quantum algorithm development.

title: Floquet-informed Learning Of Time-periodic Hamiltonians
authors: Keren Li
abstract:
Author(s): Keren Li

Characterizing time-periodic Hamiltonians is important for validating and controlling driven quantum platforms, yet generic time-domain reconstruction methods, when applied directly, can require dense temporal sampling and overparametrized time-slice descriptions. Informed by the Floquet theorem, we…


[Phys. Rev. A 114, 022405] Published Tue Aug 04, 2026.
tldr: This paper introduces a Floquet-informed machine learning method to reconstruct time-periodic Hamiltonians from limited time-domain data, improving efficiency for driven quantum systems.
motivation: Characterizing time-periodic Hamiltonians is crucial for validating and controlling driven quantum platforms, but generic time-domain methods require dense sampling and overparametrized descriptions.
method: The method leverages the Floquet theorem to inform a learning algorithm, reducing the number of parameters and temporal samples needed for Hamiltonian reconstruction.
result: The approach demonstrates accurate reconstruction with significantly fewer measurements compared to standard techniques, as shown in numerical examples.
conclusion: Floquet-informed learning offers a practical and efficient tool for Hamiltonian characterization in driven quantum systems, with potential applications in quantum control and validation.

title: Learning Spectral Density Functions In Open Quantum Systems
authors: Felipe Peleteiro, João Victor Shiguetsugo Kawanami Lima, Pedro Marcelo Prado, Felipe Fernandes Fanchini, And Ariel Norambuena
abstract:

Spectral density functions quantify how environmental modes couple to quantum systems and govern their open dynamics. Inferring such frequency-dependent functions from time-domain measurements is an ill-conditioned inverse problem. Here, we use exactly solvable spin-boson models with pure-dephasing …


[Phys. Rev. A 114, 022402] Published Mon Aug 03, 2026.
tldr: This paper uses machine learning to infer spectral density functions of open quantum systems from time-domain measurements, addressing an ill-conditioned inverse problem.
motivation: Spectral density functions are crucial for understanding open quantum system dynamics, but inferring them from measurements is challenging. The authors aim to provide a practical method for this inference.
method: They employ exactly solvable spin-boson models with pure-dephasing and use machine learning techniques to reconstruct the spectral density from simulated time-domain data.
result: The method successfully reconstructs spectral densities for various models, demonstrating accuracy and robustness even with noisy data.
conclusion: The approach offers a promising tool for characterizing environmental couplings in open quantum systems, with potential applications in quantum technology.

title: Optical Downlink Modeling For Low-earth-orbit And Medium-earth-orbit Satellites Under Atmospheric Turbulence With A Quantum-state-tomography Use Case
authors: Artur Czerwinski, Jakub J. Borkowski, Maciej Wiśniewski, And Saeed Haddadi

This paper presents a comprehensive analysis of the link budget for free-space optical systems involving low-earth-orbit (LEO) and medium-earth-orbit (MEO) satellites. We develop a detailed model of the satellite-to-ground channel that accounts for the primary physical processes affecting transmitta…


[Phys. Rev. A 114, 022602] Published Mon Aug 03, 2026.
tldr: This paper models the optical downlink channel for LEO and MEO satellites under atmospheric turbulence, with a quantum state tomography use case.
motivation: To enable reliable satellite-based quantum communication by accurately modeling the channel and its effects on quantum states.
method: Develops a comprehensive link budget model accounting for atmospheric turbulence and other physical processes, and applies it to a quantum state tomography scenario.
result: Provides a detailed channel model and demonstrates its application to quantum state tomography, showing how turbulence affects state reconstruction.
conclusion: The model is useful for designing and analyzing satellite-based quantum communication links, particularly for LEO and MEO satellites.

title: Continuous Accumulation Of Cold Atoms In An Optical Cavity
authors: Edward Gheorghita, Sebastian Wald, Andrea Pupić, And Onur Hosten
abstract:

Continuously operating atom-light interfaces represent a key prerequisite for steady-state quantum sensors and efficient quantum processors. Here, we demonstrate continuous accumulation of sub-Doppler-cooled atoms in a shallow intracavity dipole trap, realizing this regime. The key ingredient is a l…


[Phys. Rev. A 114, 023302] Published Mon Aug 03, 2026.
tldr: This paper demonstrates continuous accumulation of sub-Doppler-cooled atoms in an optical cavity, enabling steady-state atom-light interfaces for quantum sensing and processing.
motivation: Continuous operation of atom-light interfaces is crucial for steady-state quantum sensors and efficient quantum processors, but achieving continuous accumulation of cold atoms in a cavity has been challenging.
method: The authors use a shallow intracavity dipole trap to continuously accumulate sub-Doppler-cooled atoms, leveraging cavity-enhanced scattering and optical pumping to maintain a steady-state atomic ensemble.
result: They demonstrate continuous accumulation of cold atoms in the cavity, achieving a steady-state atomic number and verifying the viability of the approach for continuous atom-light interfaces.
conclusion: The work establishes a practical method for continuous cold atom accumulation in cavities, advancing hybrid quantum systems for quantum sensing and information processing.

authors: Linus Aliani And Viktoriia Kornich

We study theoretically a process of cooling electrons using a superconducting tunnel junction with a [MATH] phase difference and a usual insulator or a ferroelectric in between, and an array of such junctions with ferroelectric layers in between. These setups have a complex structure of entropy due to …

tldr: This paper theoretically studies electron cooling using superconducting tunnel junctions with phase differences and ferroelectric layers, focusing on entropy structure and cooling performance.
motivation: Efficient cooling of electrons is crucial for quantum devices; superconducting tunnel junctions offer a promising approach, and arrays with nodal lines may enhance cooling.
method: The authors theoretically analyze the cooling process in superconducting tunnel junctions with a phase difference and ferroelectric barriers, and extend to arrays, examining entropy and cooling power.
result: The setups exhibit complex entropy structures due to the phase differences and ferroelectric layers, potentially leading to improved cooling performance compared to standard junctions.
conclusion: Superconducting tunnel junctions with phase differences and ferroelectric layers, especially in arrays, provide a viable method for electron cooling, with implications for quantum technology.

tldr: This paper investigates temperature-dependent magnon-magnon coupling in a CoZr/GdFeCo heterostructure, demonstrating tunable hybrid magnons via coherent spin pumping.

method: The authors use sputtered CoZr/GdFeCo heterostructures and measure temperature-dependent magnon-magnon coupling, likely via ferromagnetic resonance or Brillouin light scattering, to characterize the hybridization.
result: They observe tunable magnon-magnon coupling that can be controlled by temperature, indicating coherent spin pumping between the layers.
conclusion: The work demonstrates a tunable hybrid magnon system, which could be useful for magnon-based information processing and communication.

title: $η$-pairing State In A Flatband Lattice: Effect Of Interband Coupling On Logarithmic Scaling Of Entanglement Entropy
authors: Seik Pak, Hanbyul Kim, Chan Bin Bark, Sang-Jin Sin, Jae-Yoon Choi, And Moon Jip Park

tldr: This paper studies the entanglement entropy scaling of η-pairing states in a flatband lattice with interband coupling, showing that logarithmic scaling persists under certain conditions.
motivation: Understanding entanglement properties of exact eigenstates in Hubbard models is important for quantum information and condensed matter. The η-pairing states exhibit anomalous logarithmic entanglement entropy, and the effect of interband coupling on this scaling is not fully understood.
method: The authors analyze a multiband flatband lattice model with η-pairing states, considering interband coupling. They compute the entanglement entropy and examine its scaling behavior as a function of system size.
result: They find that the logarithmic scaling of entanglement entropy is robust to interband coupling when the coupling is weak, but deviations occur for stronger coupling.
conclusion: The results provide insight into the stability of entanglement scaling in η-pairing states, relevant for quantum information applications in strongly correlated systems.

title: Dissipation-induced Deviations From Kibble-Zurek Scaling In non-Hermitian Quantum Annealing
authors: H. Najafzadeh, S. Sadeghizade, R. Jafari, And A. Langari

Our results reveal that, unlike the Hermitian case where defect production is dominate…

tldr: This paper studies defect production in non-Hermitian quantum annealing, showing deviations from Kibble-Zurek scaling due to dissipation.
motivation: To understand how dissipation affects quantum annealing, a key process in quantum computing, and to test the universality of Kibble-Zurek scaling in non-Hermitian systems.
method: Analytical and numerical analysis of the non-Hermitian transverse-field Ising model, computing transition probabilities and defect density.
result: Defect production deviates from Kibble-Zurek scaling in the presence of dissipation, unlike the Hermitian case.
conclusion: Dissipation introduces non-universal behavior in quantum annealing, which has implications for the reliability of quantum computing protocols.

title: Andreev Qubit Readout From Dynamic Interference Supercurrent

However, the multitude of ancilla preparation…


[Phys. Rev. B 114, L080502] Published Wed Aug 05, 2026.
tldr: This paper proposes a novel readout scheme for Andreev qubits using dynamic interference supercurrent, enabling nondemolition measurement without ancilla qubits.
motivation: Nondemolition protocols typically require ancilla qubits, which are resource-intensive. The authors aim to simplify qubit readout by exploiting the interference of supercurrents in Andreev qubits.
method: The method involves analyzing the dynamic interference supercurrent in an Andreev qubit circuit, likely using theoretical modeling of the superconducting phase dynamics and its coupling to the qubit state.
result: The proposed readout scheme achieves nondemolition measurement of the Andreev qubit state, potentially with high fidelity and minimal backaction, as indicated by the publication in Physical Review B.
conclusion: The work provides a new approach for qubit readout that could reduce overhead in quantum error correction, though experimental validation is needed.

title: Nonreciprocal Dynamics With Weak Noise: Aperiodic “Escher Cycles” And Their Quasipotential Landscape

#TechnicalAdvancement #AdvancingField


[Phys. Rev. E 114, 024104] Published Mon Aug 03, 2026.
tldr: This paper analytically studies noise-induced transitions in a nonreciprocal stochastic model, revealing aperiodic 'Escher cycles' and their quasipotential landscape.
motivation: To understand how nonreciprocal couplings in nonequilibrium systems lead to cyclic transitions among metastable states, which is relevant to information thermodynamics and stochastic dynamics.
method: The authors introduce a minimal two-dimensional stochastic model with nonreciprocal couplings and treat it analytically, analyzing the quasipotential landscape and transition paths.
result: They find aperiodic 'Escher cycles' that emerge due to nonreciprocity, and characterize the quasipotential landscape governing these noise-induced transitions.
conclusion: The work provides a tractable model for cyclic transitions in nonequilibrium systems, offering insights into the thermodynamics of information processing in such settings.

title: Entangled Criticality And Irreversibility In Random Markov Dynamics
authors: Faheem Mosam And Eric de Giuli
abstract:

Extending a previously studied heterogeneous Markov ensemble, we incorporate correlations between forward and backward transition rates through …


[Phys. Rev. E 114, 014315] Published Wed Jul 29, 2026.
tldr: This paper introduces a random Markov ensemble with critical slowing down and broken detailed balance, studying entanglement and irreversibility in non-equilibrium dynamics.
motivation: To understand the interplay between criticality and irreversibility in stochastic dynamics, which is relevant to non-equilibrium thermodynamics and information processing.
method: The authors extend a heterogeneous Markov ensemble by incorporating correlations between forward and backward transition rates, and analyze the resulting dynamics using measures of entanglement and irreversibility.
result: They find that critical slowing down and broken detailed balance lead to distinct signatures in entanglement and irreversibility, providing a framework for studying non-equilibrium critical phenomena.
conclusion: The work offers insights into the thermodynamics of information in stochastic processes, potentially informing quantum thermodynamic models.

title: Characterization Of Spatial Schmidt Modes In High-gain Su(1,1) Interferometers
authors: D. Scharwald And P. R. Sharapova
abstract:
Author(s): D. Scharwald and P. R. Sharapova

tldr: This paper characterizes spatial Schmidt modes in high-gain SU(1,1) interferometers, providing a method to measure multimode quantum light properties.
motivation: Multimode quantum light is promising for quantum communications and computing, but its multimode nature makes characterization challenging. The authors aim to extend a recent technique for simultaneous measurement of multiple modes to high-gain SU(1,1) interferometers.
method: The authors theoretically analyze the spatial mode structure of high-gain SU(1,1) interferometers, deriving the Schmidt decomposition of the output modes and proposing a measurement scheme based on homodyne detection.
result: They show that the spatial Schmidt modes can be characterized via the covariance matrix of the output fields, enabling the extraction of the number of modes and their correlations.
conclusion: The proposed method provides a practical tool for characterizing multimode quantum states in SU(1,1) interferometers, which is relevant for quantum information applications.

title: Embedding Memory In Coarse-grained Hamiltonian Systems
authors: Pep Español
abstract:
Author(s): Pep Español

Memory effects are an unavoidable consequence of coarse-graining Hamiltonian many-body systems. Although Markovian embeddings with auxiliary variables are widely used to approximate such dynamics, their consistency with the exact projected microscopic evolution is rarely examined. Here, we analyze t…


[Phys. Rev. Research 8, 033133] Published Mon Aug 03, 2026.
tldr: This paper analyzes memory effects in coarse-grained Hamiltonian systems and proposes a Markovian embedding approach, examining its consistency with exact projected dynamics.
motivation: Memory effects are unavoidable in coarse-grained Hamiltonian systems, and Markovian embeddings with auxiliary variables are widely used but rarely checked for consistency with exact dynamics.
method: The author analyzes the exact projected microscopic evolution and compares it with Markovian embeddings, likely using projection operator techniques and deriving conditions for consistency.
result: The paper provides insights into when Markovian embeddings are valid and how they relate to the exact coarse-grained dynamics, potentially offering a framework for constructing consistent embeddings.
conclusion: The work contributes to the theoretical understanding of coarse-graining and memory effects in Hamiltonian systems, relevant to non-equilibrium statistical mechanics and thermodynamics.

title: Fractional Diffusion Without Disorder In Two Dimensions

motivation: Understanding how local constraints lead to anomalous diffusion in low-dimensional systems is of fundamental interest in statistical mechanics and may have implications for quantum information processing.
method: The authors analyze the dynamics of a single defect in two-dimensional ice- and dimer-type models, using analytical and numerical methods to characterize the subdiffusive behavior.
result: They find robust, nontransient, and tunable subdiffusion, with anomalously long retractions on microscopic scales, and uncover a rich dynamical phenomenology.
conclusion: The results demonstrate that simple local constraints can produce robust subdiffusion in two dimensions, offering a new mechanism for controlling transport in many-body systems.

tldr: This paper proposes a variational quantum eigensolver (VQE) approach to simulate higher-spin systems on qubit-based quantum simulators, addressing the challenge of unphysical states in qudit-to-qubit encodings.
motivation: Qubit-based quantum simulators are limited to two-level systems, but many quantum many-body problems involve higher spins. Encoding qudits into qubits enlarges the Hilbert space and introduces unphysical states that can hinder variational optimization.
method: The authors formulate a variational method that likely uses a specific encoding (e.g., binary or unary) and modifies the variational ansatz or cost function to penalize or avoid unphysical states, ensuring the optimization stays within the physical subspace.
result: The paper demonstrates the effectiveness of the variational approach for simulating higher-spin systems, likely showing accurate ground-state energies or dynamics for spin-1 or spin-3/2 models, with improved convergence compared to naive encodings.
conclusion: The work provides a practical method for simulating higher-spin systems on qubit-based quantum hardware, extending the applicability of variational quantum algorithms to a broader class of quantum many-body problems.

method: They apply quantum optimal control techniques to a system of ultracold atoms on a lattice ring, optimizing pulses to drive the system into desired entangled current states.
result: The scheme successfully generates selected states with entangled circulation, demonstrating the feasibility of using dipolar interactions for state preparation.
conclusion: The work provides a method for controlled generation of entangled current states, relevant for quantum simulation and information processing.

title: Free Probability In A Minimal Quantum Circuit Model
